ast_scope_check: Whole module matches baseline after restoring only flush_exports; the safe projection and other production AST nodes are unchanged. Both selected wrapper ASTs match original fresh baseline before patch.
compatibility: Append-before-mark, durable-flush-before-commit, no-rows reporting, failure identity, and best-effort post-commit suppression are preserved. Only flush_exports changed semantically; the safe projection wrapper is extracted for its existing caller contract and is unchanged. No full-suite compatibility claim; an existing storage test expects append to raise on projection failure and conflicts with the already-current best-effort contract.
execution_scope: The new shell imports no target module and extracts exactly two complete RuntimeStore methods into a base-free class. All database, marker, count SQL, log append, durable flush, auxiliary lookup, committed-export adapter, and Markdown operations are fake. Payload/digest/record values are opaque. No actual SQL, marker journal, export filesystem, archive, permissions, evidence/admission, identity, model or production operations execute. Prior bounded fake regression files run separately under their established scope.
test_delivery: The new standalone shell intentionally runs only with an explicit source path and expected SHA-256; it is not auto-discovered as a normal pytest test. Standard-library runner only; full pytest suite not run.
limits: This demonstrates wrapper ownership/order with opaque fakes, not real SQLite, durability, marker/journal, admission, identity, evidence or archive correctness.
The new shell requires explicit source/hash arguments and is not auto-discovered by pytest.
Existing storage test source expectation conflicts with current best-effort append behavior; it was not run or modified.
